items.why: viz3d.js registers exactly two providers, bodyparts3d and svg. There is NO procedural provider, so a model built by this task has nothing to plug into and cannot reach a student. This must be built before any scene can move past 'planned'. Build it as a third provider that resolves a structure key to a builder module under viz-training/models/, mirroring how bodyparts3d resolves a key to an STL. Do not change the two existing providers. Do not touch the frozen Smart-Drill engine. Bump the sw.js CACHE version, reading its CURRENT value first — another session moves it.
items.reviewed_by: Frank + session (built by hand, not by the build task — an unproven task should not make its first-ever run an engine change)
built_notes: viz3d.js registers 'procedural' beside bodyparts3d and svg. Same adapter contract: resolve(s) and load(T,s) -> {mesh, reason}. The two existing providers are untouched.
Ref shape is a plain string like bodyparts3d's: refs.procedural = "<model>#<part>", optionally "...@<t>". An object {model,part,t} also parses.

Models live under MEDBANK_CONFIG.MODEL_BASE (default ./models3d/) and register window.MB3D_MODELS[id] = {LAYERS, build, FULL}. render-kit.js is loaded once, before any model, because it reads window.THREE at evaluation.

ONE STRUCTURE, ONE MESH: the engine reads m.geometry directly for highlight patches, anchors and bounding boxes, so a Group would break it. The adapter merges every mesh carrying the key into one geometry and drops silhouette shells.

PROVEN, not assumed: all 8 parts of cardiac-looping resolve with correct triangle counts; unknown part -> 'none'; absent ref -> 'none'; missing model file -> 'failed'; t=0 and t=1 give different geometry; rendered through the app's own lighting rig.

A bug this testing caught: the adapter first built with {}, so any layer behind an option flag (the endocardial tube) came back as 'none' — 'the corpus has no model of this' — which was a lie about a model sitting right there. Models now declare FULL and the adapter builds the complete set.
known_gaps: t is per scene or per structure, NOT per view. A scene cannot yet animate through its own stages with an op — that belongs in the op dispatcher, not the adapter.
Procedural models are in their own units; BodyParts3D meshes are anatomical millimetres. A scene must not mix the two providers until something reconciles scale.

NOT PROVEN / NEW OPEN DEFECT, MINE, AND I COULD NOT SOLVE IT OUT. THE ATRIUM HANGS OFF THE EMBRYO'S LEFT: atrium centroid x +1.14 at t=1 (the previous solve had +0.30), sinus +0.66. The common atrium at day 28 straddles the median plane; a centroid a whole chamber-radius off it is not that. It is visible in the render before it is visible in any number, and NOTHING in the review's test set constrains it — RENDER-STANDARD's 'the unlisted place is the one nobody checks', arriving one solve after it was written. I added the constraints as J (|atrium x| small) and K (|sinus x| small) and re-solved TWICE: at J<=0.35 the best candidate fails H65, I and J and is unstable; relaxed to J<=0.55 it converges to I -0.012 / J 0.823. It will not hold the ventricle LEFT and the atrium MIDLINE at the same time. My reading: with four Gaussian bends each carrying ONE plane, the atrium lies between the sinoatrial and AV bends and its lateral position is not independently controllable — this needs a degree of freedom the curvature model does not have, not a better search. I SHIPPED the candidate that satisfies every condition the review asked for and left J and K failing, rather than sacrificing I, H or C to a constraint I invented this run. That is the call I am least sure of and the first thing to overturn if a reviewer disagrees.

THE MODEL GAINED TWO FREEDOMS. (a) Each bend's plane now varies along its own width: psi_j(u) = psi[j] + tw[j]*z, torsion distributed rather than lumped, so a bend can enter in one plane and leave in another. (b) A FIFTH BEND at u=0.055, the confluence where the horns join the sinus venosus — NOT a segment boundary; the five segments still divide at the four named waists. Evidence four were not enough rather than assumption: J and K were ALREADY in the solver at |x|<=0.55 and the shipped params measured 1.10 and 0.73, and two independent searches from different seeds made the SAME trade. A penalty still large at the optimum after a global search is a missing degree of freedom, not a bad seed.

FIVE OF THE TWELVE TESTS WERE MEASURING SOMETHING OTHER THAN THEIR OWN PROSE, and three of those five I introduced this round while fixing the first two. On this item the tests fail more often than the geometry does.

TEST B' WAS AN ARGMAX AND THAT COST FIVE REJECTED CANDIDATES. Its second clause read 'the max |x| of the bulboventricular centreline is on the -x side' — discontinuous. Once I puts the ventricle firmly left and F the bulbus firmly right the two reach comparable |x| and the SIGN flips with integration density: -0.619 at NSEG 140 and 300, +0.619 at 600, on a curve whose every other measure moved by under 0.003. Five candidates were rejected as 'on a bifurcation' on the strength of that flip; the curve was stable, the statistic was not. It is now the BULBUS's own convexity (weighted mean x minus the mean of its endpoints), measured over the bulbus alone because the bulbus bows right (-0.055) while the ventricle bows left (+0.159) and averaging both reports the loop SINISTRAL (+0.319). Stable to 0.002 across 140/300/600.

FINDING 9 CANNOT BE SATISFIED AS LITERALLY STATED, AND THAT IS PROVED TWICE. (a) On SEGMENTS: the ventricle and bulbus segments are contiguous, sharing the station at the bulboventricular sulcus, so their boxes must overlap by at least 2r in EVERY axis for every curve. r(0.660)=0.3931 at t=1, and a candidate whose limbs are otherwise completely clear measures an x-overlap of 0.786 — exactly 2r to three decimals. The review's '1.05 units of overlap on chambers about 1.56 wide' is very largely that shared waist, which is the one place the two limbs are REQUIRED to touch because it is the groove between them. (b) On BODIES, which is what the review's own words ask for: the ventricle body ends at u=0.593 and the bulbus body begins at u=0.683 — 0.808 units of ARC — while their peak radii sum to 1.156. No path of length 0.808 separates two points by 1.156. Bound: gap <= -0.348 at t=1, assuming every unit of arc goes into pure x displacement, which a tube that must also turn cannot do. The chambers are larger than the gap between them, and that IS the anatomy: dilated chambers, short sulcus.

WHAT TEST L BECAME: transverse separation of the two limbs' CENTRES over the distance at which the two chambers would be exactly tangent. 1.0 = just touching. MEASURED 0.919 at t=1, floor 0.85. Strongest form of finding 9 that does not require a curve which cannot exist. Gated at t=1 ONLY because finding 9's own source says 'AFTER looping'; what view 4 claims at t=0.65 is the weaker 'side by side rather than one BEHIND the other', which is test H65 and H65 IS gated. L65=0.698 is reported so the separation can be watched growing rather than taken on trust.

A NEW RENDER-KIT BUG AFFECTING EVERY MODEL IN THE CORPUS, found by the probe written for finding 4. sweptShell's flat end caps for a SOLID tube (every tubeAlong — every vein, artery, rod and tick we draw) went through emitter().tri, which corrects nothing; both branches were written by reasoning about which way the ring runs and both were backwards. MEASURED: 24 of 24 cap triangles on a plain tubeAlong wound against their own supplied normal. It never showed because caps sit inside the hull count and materials are DoubleSide — RENDER-STANDARD 2.1's own description of itself, in the one code path that had bypassed the fix. FIXED: emitter().triN(p1,p2,p3,n) decides the order from the geometry. The model's local emitTri is gone with it (section 6). New rule and its ray-cast check written into RENDER-STANDARD as 2.4b.

FINDING 4 FIXED IN THE KIT: VizKit.domeCap closes a terminal ring with a rounded dome sharing the tube's exact cross-section. BOTH ends are domed — the cranial one had been worked around a round earlier by pointing view 9 away from it, which closed no hole. A camera is not a fix; it only moves the unlisted place. PROVEN by ray-cast from five cameras (anterior t=0.42/0.65/1.00, from above, from below): 0 of 8661 first hits face away from the camera. Before the fix the same probe found 16/29/5/86/14; the 'from below' hits were the dorsal aortae, which nobody had named.

FINDING 5: the median-plane reference rebuilt, 84024 px visible at t=1 = 29.2% of the subject (was 125 px, 0.081%). NOTE WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG: a translucent quad IN the median plane is seen exactly edge-on by an anterior camera, because the plane contains that camera's view direction. What a plane gives such a camera is its TRACE, and the old rod's fault was never that it was a line — it was that the line sat at z=0, buried inside a loop reaching z=+1.68. Now: translucent quad (carries it in oblique and lateral views) PLUS its ventral edge as a solid rod standing clear IN FRONT of the loop, with the forward reach measured off the built curve at each t.

FINDING 6: the bends now have STAGGERED ONSETS — bulboventricular leads, then bulbotruncal, atrioventricular, sinoatrial last, which is why the inflow limb's climb is the THIRD movement. At t=0.42 the bulboventricular bend has done 59% of its turn and the sinoatrial climb 1%. New scene stage _ab at t=0.42; view 3 re-pointed to it, view 4 keeps _b, so the two views are two different pictures of two different moments. THE STAGGER IS A REDISTRIBUTION, NOT A THROTTLE: scaling every bend by its ramp does nothing (lambda is solved against the tether and cancels a common factor, and where it could not cancel it — t=0.25, one bend awake — it pinned at its cap, the very bifurcation this model's notes warn about, arriving as a side effect of an unrelated fix). Scaling the tether instead made the early loop a slack tube, the wrong mechanism. The ramps now set only the SHARE of curvature each bend carries, renormalised; every ramp is 1 at t=1 so the day-28 loop is untouched.

THE STAGGER'S OWN TEST WAS WRONG FIRST TIME, in this item's signature way: it divided by the day-28 value alone, and on a straight tube the atrium starts BELOW the ventricle, so 'how much of the climb is done' read -0.8 for a heart that had simply not climbed yet. Both figures are now fractions of the total change, 0 at t=0 and 1 at t=1 by construction, and TWO-SIDED — a one-sided floor is satisfied by a loop that OVERSHOOTS mid-process and comes back, a defect this file already records rejecting a candidate for.

TEST D's OVERLAP CEILING WAS MY OWN ERROR, not a target the geometry missed. I wrote DOV=0.62 alongside a centroid floor of 0.35, and the two are not independent: with these extents a 0.62 ceiling silently DEMANDS a centroid separation of about 0.55 of mean height — far stricter than the 0.35 the standards gap sets, and stricter than anything stated anywhere. Two conditions written separately were one condition written twice, the tighter of them hidden. DOV is now 0.75, the tightest ceiling consistent with a 0.35 floor, and still a very large change from the 97.8% overlap the review measured. Measured: Dfrac 0.420, Dov 0.719 on real mesh.

A TOOL BUG IN solve-cardiac-torsion.mjs THAT ITS OWN HEADER WARNS ABOUT. It rounded the winning parameters to four decimals and handed them straight on. A candidate refined to a robust penalty of 16.8 came out of that rounding with a 140-vs-300 drift of 12.57 — A=+0.962 at NSEG 140 and -0.037 at 300, the loop INVERTED — and printed as an answer; it was caught only because the MUSTS line disagreed with the penalty, which is luck, not a check. The tool now rounds, RE-SCORES, and backs off to more decimals, rejecting outright anything needing more than six. Two candidates this round genuinely needed six decimals; one needed eight and was rejected. Separately, the stability verdict compared only 300 vs 600 while claiming to catch bifurcations — it now compares 140/300/600 and reports whichever pair disagrees.

findings: 1. THE ATRIUM AND THE SINUS VENOSUS FINISH ENTIRELY ON THE EMBRYO'S LEFT. The build task declared this itself and could not solve it out; it is confirmed, and the BOUNDING BOX makes it worse than the centroid the builder reported. Measured on real mesh vertices at t=1 (+x = LEFT): atrium x spans +0.151 to +2.017 — it NEVER REACHES THE MEDIAN PLANE, let alone straddles it; sinus x spans -0.085 to +1.716, 95.3% of its width on the left. Centroids atrium +1.101, sinus +0.729 (the builder's centreline figures were +1.14 and +0.66). Why it is a teaching error and not a cosmetic one: the common atrium at day 28 straddles the midline, and the sinus venosus is the RIGHT-sided inflow whose right horn becomes the sinus venarum — the smooth posterior wall of the right atrium and the reason SVC and IVC drain where they do. A student who learns this picture puts the systemic venous inflow on the left. Test J (|atrium x| small) and K (|sinus x| small) exist in the builder's own notes and both FAIL.

2. THE ATRIA ARE NOT ABOVE THE VENTRICLES — NEW, AND NOTHING IN THE TEST SET CONSTRAINS IT. At t=1 the atrium spans y -2.714 to -0.514 (height 2.200) and the ventricle spans y -3.100 to -0.563 (height 2.538). THE OVERLAP IS 2.152, WHICH IS 97.8% OF THE ATRIUM'S OWN VERTICAL EXTENT. Centroid separation D = +0.351, i.e. 16% of the atrium's height. Test D asks only 'atrium y - ventricle y > 0' and +0.351 satisfies it, so the model asserts the relation on every build while the picture does not show it. This is the THIRD movement, which is the entire subject of view 5 ('Movement three — the atria climb up behind') and the second line of view 6's three-sentence exam drill ('atria side by side behind and above them'). For contrast the DORSAL half of the same claim is legible and fine: C = -0.80 with only 58% z-overlap. It is specifically the vertical separation that is missing. Note also that in the world frame the atrium and sinus DESCEND between t=0 and t=1 (atrium y -1.060 to -1.548, sinus -2.249 to -2.702) while the venous pole is nailed at y -2.887, so on screen nothing climbs; the relation only improves because the ventricle descends faster.

3. THE VENTRICLE FINISHES ON THE MEDIAN PLANE, NOT TO THE LEFT — TEST I PASSES ON THE SIGN AND THE PICTURE DOES NOT. Ventricle centroid x = +0.070 on a chamber 1.329 wide: FIVE PER CENT of its own width. Round 2 wrote I as 'ventricle centroid x > 0' and the round-2 rework solved to +0.070, which satisfies it exactly and invisibly. View 4 says 'the primitive ventricle moves backwards and to the left'; views 6 and 8 depend on the future left ventricle being visibly left-posterior, because that is what makes view 8's 'the morphological right ventricle on the left' a legible contrast rather than a caption. A student sees a ventricle in the middle. THIS IS THE SAME FAILURE MODE ROUND 2 FOUND TWICE (finding 2, a test that did not test its own `must` string; finding 4, a test that locked in a defect) NOW RECURRING IN A TEST ROUND 2 ITSELF WROTE. See standards_gap_round_3: the fix is a magnitude floor, not another sign test.

4. THE SINUS VENOSUS IS AN OPEN PIPE AT ITS CAUDAL END, AND IT IS VISIBLE IN VIEWS 3 AND 4. sweptShell() closes every segment with ANNULAR END CAPS, and OVERLAP = 0.006 hides the caps at the four internal waists — but the tube has TWO TERMINAL ends with no neighbour to hide behind. gaps[10] records that view 9 was tried from ABOVE and rejected because it 'looks straight down the truncus and shows its open lumen — the one thing RENDER-STANDARD says must never be visible'. The caudal end of the SINUS has exactly the same cap and was never worked around: it is plainly visible from the ANTERIOR camera at stage _b, which is the camera and the stage that views 3 and 4 both use. Wall ring and lit inner surface are unambiguous in _review-2026-09-10-r3-cardiac-looping/crop-sinus-b.png. The veins cross the opening without plugging it. This is the same defect at the other end of the same tube, avoided at one end by choosing a camera and left exposed at the other — the unlisted place. FIX: do not solve it with a camera. Either carry the sinus caudally into the vein confluence so the veins close it, or cap the terminal ends with a rounded dome rather than an annulus.

5. THE MEDIAN-PLANE REFERENCE IS 96.5% OCCLUDED IN THE ONLY VIEW THAT USES IT. The midline is a rod of RADIUS 0.030 plus three ventral ticks that reach only z = +1.15, while the heart's ventral surface at t=1 reaches z = +1.684 — so the rod lies BEHIND the ventricle and bulbus from the anterior camera. Measured by differencing view 9's own camera with and without midline:true — midline pixels if nothing occluded it 3,525; midline pixels ACTUALLY VISIBLE 125; that is 0.081% of the subject's 154,711 pixels. The reference was added in round 1 (finding 12) specifically so that 'mirror image about the median plane' would be a visible claim rather than a caption, and view 9 HIGHLIGHTs it at intensity 0.6. It does not survive its own view. FIX: draw the plane as a translucent quad in the median plane, or bring the ticks forward past z = +1.7 and thicken the rod, and re-measure the visible pixel count rather than assuming.

6. VIEWS 3 AND 4 NARRATE TWO SEQUENTIAL MOVEMENTS OVER ONE FROZEN STAGE, SO NEITHER MOVEMENT IS VISIBLE AS A MOVEMENT. Both views draw stage _b (t = 0.65) with an IDENTICAL structure set and an identical camera, differing only in which structure is highlighted. They pass the no-duplicate-frame rule as written, and they are not pixel-identical. But all four Gaussian bends grow together with t, so NO value of t separates movement one from movement two: at t = 0.65 the ventricle has already swung dorsally and left whatever view 3's title says, and by stage _c all three movements are complete. A student told 'the first movement is the one that names the loop' is looking at a picture in which the second and third have already happened. gaps[2] declares the per-structure-t mechanism but not this consequence. FIX, and it does not need the engine: give the four bends STAGGERED ONSETS in t so that the bulboventricular bend leads and the sinoatrial bend follows, then add a stage between _a and _b. Do not fix it by re-pointing _b — that was tried in round 1 and the movements still coincide.

7. STATED POSITIVELY — ROUND 2'S FOUR FINDINGS ARE ALL GENUINELY FIXED, RE-VERIFIED WITHOUT THE BUILDER'S PROVERS. The build task asked for exactly this ('prove-mirror-chirality.mjs is not independent evidence — I wrote both the fix and its prover'), so it was done in a harness written for this review. FINDING 1, the mirror: every vertex of all ELEVEN parts matches a true reflect-X at 1.0000 and rot-Y-180 at 0.0000-0.0020, with identical vertex counts; the signed volume recomputed here from MESH centroids (not the centreline tetrahedron mirrorProof() uses) is D -0.05029 / L +0.05029, ratio exactly -1.0000, where round 2 measured +1.0000. In the picture, view 9's mirror against view 6's D-loop is a clean left-right flip at the same size, against round 2's measured 79% of width. FINDINGS 3 AND 4: all nine acceptance tests pass and are stable across integration density — nseg 140/300/600 agree to 0.003, worst drift 300->600 = 0.003, and the builder's shipped numbers reproduce exactly. FINDING 5: peri_a on view 1 and peri_c on view 6, both present. FINDING 2 was the reviewer's own correction and is preserved. Finding 6 (cross-item) is dissolved as the builder said.

8. ANSWERING THE BUILD TASK'S DIRECT QUESTION, BECAUSE IT ASKED THE REVIEW TO DECIDE AND IT WAS RIGHT NOT TO DECIDE ALONE. The question was: 'whether the fix is a richer curvature model (a bend whose plane varies along its own width, or a fifth bend) or whether test I should be weakened instead'. THE ANSWER IS: DO NOT WEAKEN I, ENRICH THE MODEL. The anatomy is determinate — the future left ventricle finishes left-posterior, the common atrium straddles the midline, the atria finish above the ventricles — so every one of findings 1, 2 and 3 has a correct answer that geometry can express, and weakening a test to fit a curvature model is the standard lowering itself to let the item pass. The builder's own diagnosis is almost certainly right: four Gaussian bends each carrying ONE plane cannot control the atrium's lateral position independently of the ventricle's, and that is a missing degree of freedom rather than a failed search. FINDINGS 1, 2 AND 3 ARE ONE SOLVE, NOT THREE PIECES OF WORK: add J (|atrium x| <= 0.35), K (|sinus x| <= 0.45) and a strengthened D and I per standards_gap_round_3, give the model the extra freedom first, and solve once. Findings 4, 5 and 6 are independent of that solve and can be done in any order.

THE PREVIOUS REVIEW REACHED THE WRONG CONCLUSION, AND SO WOULD A FOURTH ROUND THAT TRUSTED IT. Round-2 finding 3 said view 4's narration is false because the geometry does not support it — measured at t=0.65, transverse separation 0.319 against antero-posterior 0.714 — and recommended the narration be rewritten or the view re-pointed. Checked against the embryology rather than against our own model: the narration is CORRECT and the MODEL is what is wrong. After looping, the bulbus cordis and primitive ventricle lie side by side HORIZONTALLY, occupying opposite sides of the pericardial cavity — the atrioventricular junction on the LEFT of the pericardial cavity and the elongated bulbus on the RIGHT — forming a cephalic/ascending limb (bulbus) and a descending limb (embryonic ventricle). Source: Review of Medical Embryology ch.115, Formation of the Heart Loop (discovery.lifemapsc.com). Wikipedia's Bulbus cordis article says the bulbus ends 'slightly to the left of the ventricle', which contradicts both our scene and that chapter — treat it as unreliable and do not resolve the conflict from it. DO NOT EDIT THE NARRATION. Fix the geometry: the two limbs must end up on opposite sides of the midline. Today the chamber bounding boxes overlap transversely by 1.05 units on chambers about 1.56 wide, i.e. almost completely, at every t — that is the defect. Acceptance G should measure limb separation against limb width (the two bodies substantially clear of one another in x), not centroid dx against centroid dy, because two overlapping bodies can have separated centroids and still not read as side by side. Whoever takes this: measure the model against the anatomy, not the anatomy against the model. That inversion is the whole finding.
items.standards_gap: RENDER-STANDARD has rules for winding, normals, colour, hulls and frame fill, and every one of them passed here. It has NOTHING that would have caught findings 1 or 2, because both are about whether the model is oriented and posed the way the anatomy says. Two rules proposed. (a) DECLARE THE AXES AND PROVE THEM. A model states its axis convention in a machine-readable field, and the check asserts it against the corpus: RIGHT is -x, LEFT is +x, CRANIAL +y, VENTRAL +z, measured from BodyParts3D right/left pairs, not from a comment. This model's comment had the sign backwards and nothing noticed. (b) A SPATIAL CLAIM IN NARRATION IS A TESTABLE ASSERTION. When a view says one part ends up behind, above, right of or inside another, that is a check against the two bounding boxes at that view's t. 'The inflow end comes to lie behind and above the ventricles' is one line of arithmetic, and it fails.

findings_round_1: 1. THE LOOP BENDS DORSALLY, NOT VENTRALLY. This is the biggest one and it is invisible in the anterior view, which is why it survived the build. Measured in world space at t=1, centroid z (model's own +z = ventral): ventricle 0 -> -1.12, bulbus 0 -> -0.82, atrium 0 -> -0.93. Every segment goes backwards. Confirmed by rendering a lateral view with axis rods drawn in: the whole heart sits on the -z side of the original tube axis (viz-training/_review-2026-09-10/diag-t1-lateral.png). View 3 is TITLED 'Movement one - the bulbus swings ventrally, caudally and to the RIGHT' and its narration says 'swings forwards, downwards and to the right'. Ventral and right are the two halves of the D-loop and only the right half is built. A student who rotates the model learns the convexity points backwards. NOT a sign flip: negating z would send the atrium ventral, which is equally wrong. It is the torsion — PSI0 = 0.26 and TAU = 1.60, the two hand-tuned constants in psi(u,t) — that has to carry the cranial limb ventral and the caudal limb dorsal. RENDER-STANDARD's own rule 'PREFER A SOLVED PARAMETER TO A TUNED ONE' applies: the amplitude is solved by bisection, but the torsion, which decides the examinable relation, is guessed. SHARPENED ON RE-CHECK, and correcting my own overstatement: it is NOT true that all three segments are wrong. Beat 4's narration wants the ventricle DORSAL and beat 5 wants the atrium dorsal and cranial, and both of those the model gets right. The relative order of the two limbs is right too — the bulbus is ventral to the ventricle at t = 1 (z -0.82 vs -1.12). Two things are wrong. The BULBUS moves dorsally from its own start (z 0 -> -0.82) while view 3 says it swings forwards, and the whole loop is displaced backwards, which is what puts the ventricle behind the atrium in finding 2. The target for the rebuild is therefore not 'flip z' but 'separate the limbs in the AP axis about an axis that does not itself travel dorsally'.

2. AT DAY 28 THE ATRIUM IS STILL BELOW THE VENTRICLE, AND IS VENTRAL TO IT. Measured at t=1: atrium y centre -0.68 vs ventricle y centre +0.51, so the inflow end is still caudal; atrium z centre -0.93 vs ventricle -1.12, so the ventricle is the more DORSAL of the two. View 5's narration says 'the inflow end comes to lie behind and above the ventricles instead of below them' and view 6 says the atria 'lie side by side behind and above them'. Both are contradicted by the geometry, and view 5 is a LATERAL view, so the student is looking straight at the contradiction while being told the opposite. This is the relation the whole adult mediastinum hangs on. Same root cause as finding 1. QUANTIFIED ON RE-CHECK: the atrium starts 1.48 units below the ventricle at t = 0 and ends 1.19 below at t = 1. The third movement closes 20% of a gap it is supposed to cross. And the AP relation is inverted at every t, worst in mid-loop: ventricle-minus-atrium z is 0.00 at t = 0, -0.33 at t = 0.4, -0.20 at t = 1, where it needs to be positive throughout.

3. THE DORSAL MESOCARDIUM NEVER BREAKS DOWN — IT JUST FADES. mesoAlpha = 1 below t=0.34 then ramps to 0 by t=0.58, and the sheet is one continuous quad strip at every t. There is no version of it with a central gap. View 2's whole teaching payoff is that gap: 'The middle of the dorsal mesocardium has already given way... The gap it leaves behind is the transverse pericardial sinus, which is why in the adult you can pass a finger behind the aorta and pulmonary trunk and in front of the atria.' Nothing in the model can show that. Worse, view 2 shows meso_a, which is 'cardiac-looping#mesocardium@0' and is LABELLED 'Dorsal mesocardium, still intact' — so the picture asserts intact while the narration says broken. And it is worse again than that: the sheet is a median-plane membrane and view 2 does not rotate, so in the anterior view it is edge-on behind the tube and invisible. View 2 renders PIXEL-IDENTICAL to view 1. FIX: build the mesocardium as two cuffs with a real gap between them once t passes the breakdown threshold, give the scene a meso_b at that t, and rotate view 2 to lateral. I did not rotate view 2 on its own — showing an intact sheet clearly under narration that says it has broken down is a worse error than showing nothing, and rotating without the model change would have shipped exactly that.

4. THE PERICARDIUM CANNOT SHOW THE ONE THING IT IS THERE FOR. It is sized from the bounding box of the heart at that same t (box = Box3().setFromObject(heartOnly), then scaled from sz), so the cavity grows with the tube. View 1's narration - the mechanical premise of the entire scene - is 'it is elongating faster than the pericardial cavity around it'. A cavity scaled to the tube can never show a tube outgrowing it. It is also drawn at opacity 0.022, which is invisible. FIX: size the cavity from the day-21 tube and hold it, or grow it on its own slower schedule, so the crowding is visible; then put it on view 1.

5. THE MODEL WILL BREAK THE PAGE WHEN A SECOND PROCEDURAL MODEL LOADS. models3d/cardiac-looping.js is not wrapped in an IIFE, so const T, const K, const C, LAYERS, L0, GROW, NSEG, NRING, WALL, JELLY, K_LOOP, K_ATRIAL, PSI0, TAU, MIRROR, POLE, SEGS, OVERLAP and every function land in the global lexical scope. neurulation.js is next in the queue and the obvious way to write it is 'const T = window.THREE' at the top, which throws SyntaxError: Identifier 'T' has already been declared and kills the whole script. items.standards_gap_round_2: RENDER-STANDARD.md would not have caught round 2's finding 1, and its own text is part of why. Section 2.1 makes reversed winding the cardinal sin, so a model author writing a mirror is pushed towards the construction trick precisely BECAUSE it leaves winding untouched — and untouched winding is the signature of a rotation. TWO RULES PROPOSED. (a) A MIRRORED VARIANT MUST BE PROVED TO BE A REFLECTION. Chirality is not implied by any check we currently run: triangle count, outward-normal fraction, negated mean x and untouched winding all pass on a 180-degree rotation, and all four were cited as proof here. The test is one line — the signed volume of four named landmark centroids must be NEGATED, not preserved — and it belongs in the model's acceptance(), asserted on the mirror build, which is the build acceptance() never touches. Add the corollary too: a genuine enantiomer MUST reverse winding, so the emitter flips through quadFlip; if a mirror needed no rendering change at all, it is not a mirror. (b) AN ACCEPTANCE TEST MUST BE TESTED AGAINST ITS OWN PROSE. Test G's must string said transverse and its implementation said hypot(transverse, antero-posterior), so the one arrangement the narration denies was counted as evidence for the arrangement it asserts, and a false claim about t = 0.65 propagated from the test into the build notes and into the scene's gaps[]. A test that grades its own homework in the wrong units is worse than no test: it launders a defect into a proof. Every id in an ACCEPTANCE block needs a negative case — a deliberately wrong input the test must reject — the way validate-scenes negative-tests its new checks.

(a) VERTEX LEVEL: every vertex of the D-loop build, transformed and matched against the mirror build — sinus, atrium, ventricle, bulbus and truncus all match rot-Y-180 (x,y,z -> -x,y,-z) at 100.0% and match a true reflect-X (x -> -x) at 0.0%. items.standards_gap_round_3: THE STANDARD HAS A GAP AND THIS IS THE THIRD ROUND IN A ROW IT HAS COST SOMETHING. Round 2 finding 2: a test whose implementation did not match its own `must` string. Round 2 finding 4: a test that asserted a defect and so locked it in. Round 3 finding 3: a test that is CORRECT and asserts the right relation, and is satisfied by a value so small the claim is invisible — ventricle x = +0.070 on a chamber 1.329 wide passes 'ventricle centroid x > 0' at 5% of its own width. Finding 2 is the same shape: D = +0.351 passes 'atrium y - ventricle y > 0' while 97.8% of the atrium's vertical extent still overlaps the ventricle's. PROPOSED RULE, for RENDER-STANDARD and for the acceptance-test convention generally: A SIGN TEST ON A SPATIAL RELATION IS NOT A TEST. Every acceptance assertion of the form 'A is left of / above / behind B' must carry a MAGNITUDE FLOOR expressed as a fraction of the relevant extent of the structures being compared — as a starting figure, a separation of at least 35% of the mean of the two structures' extents along that axis, so that the relation is legible in the picture and not merely true in the arithmetic. Sign-only tests should be written as `> 0.35 * meanExtent`, not `> 0`, and any existing sign test should be read as UNPROVEN until it carries a floor. The deeper rule, which is what the three rounds actually demonstrate: A TEST THAT CAN BE SATISFIED WITHOUT THE PICTURE CHANGING IS NOT MEASURING WHAT THE NARRATION CLAIMS. The narration is about what a student can SEE; the tests should be too. Second, smaller gap: the review standard says 'console clean — no errors, no warnings' but nothing says a self-check must distinguish CANNOT MEASURE from MEASURED AND WRONG. items.why: MEASURED IN THE LIVE PLAYER, 2026-09-10, by reading the canvas pixels view by view. The camera is fitted ONCE to every structure the scene loads, and never refits when a view shows only a subset. So a view that isolates parts leaves the subject at roughly half the linear size it should be. On the cardiac-looping scene: views showing the whole embryo fill 67-74% of the canvas height, but view 9 (D-loop vs L-loop, 4 parts) fills 30% and view 10 (dextrocardia, 2 parts) fills 30% x 16% — 3.0% of the canvas lit. This is RENDER-STANDARD's first standing rule, THE SUBJECT FILLS THE FRAME, failing inside the player rather than in a model.
items.note: MOVED AHEAD OF engine__per-view-t on 2026-09-10. Per-view-t makes FUTURE process scenes tidier; this fixes framing in the 71 scenes already in front of students. Measured by the review task: with a per-view refit, cardiac-looping views 9 and 10 go from 30% to 84% and 76% of frame width. Bigger payoff, smaller change, and it repairs shipped work rather than unshipped work. Not a cardiac-looping bug — it is the player's framing, so it affects EVERY scene that isolates, including the 71 ready BodyParts3D ones. Fit to the bounding box of the VISIBLE meshes after each view's ops have run, and ease the camera rather than jumping. Beware the opposite failure: refitting on a single small part will zoom so far in that the student loses all context, so clamp how far a refit may travel from the whole-scene fit.

findings: 1 · REGRESSION, MEASURED, THE BLOCKER. frameView() frames on state.only, but state.only is only what ISOLATE_REGION/COMPARE_STRUCTURES singled out — not what the view is about. A view that isolates one group then names more (SHOW_STRUCTURE after the isolate, HIGHLIGHT_STRUCTURE, SHOW_RELATIONSHIP from/to) now pushes the rest off the stage. At rest, 1008x440, before -> after: gross__kidney-posterior-abdominal-wall__kidney view 6 'Reading the clinic off the anatomy' 58.0%h/18.6% area -> 100.0h x 94.1w, 72.9% area, clipped, geometric fill 2765% (a corner projecting from BEHIND the camera); neuroanatomy__cerebrum-gross-lobes__cerebral-hemispheres-lobes view 10 -> 100.0h, clipped, fill 87005%; gross__back-vertebral-column__vertebral-column view 4 'Body in front, canal behind' 28.6h -> 100.0h x 100.0w; gross__back-vertebral-column__intervertebral-disc view 2 'One joint, two bones' -> clipped, L5 cut off at NDC y=1.03 while the narration says 'two vertebral bodies with one pad between them'. Six views across three scenes now land at exactly 100.0% of frame height; none did before. See _review-2026-09-10-r3/kidney-view06-after.png — the ureter the narration follows to the bladder runs off the bottom edge.

2 · THE FIX, TRIED AND REVERTED BY THE REVIEWER — DO NOT RE-DERIVE IT FROM SCRATCH. Frame on state.only UNION every key the view's ops name after it isolates. I patched subjectBox() that way and measured: kidney v6 goes 100.0h/clipped -> 66.4h/not clipped and intervertebral-disc v2's clipping goes away, but kidney v3 gets worse (44.8h -> 100.0h, 82.9% area) and kidney v2 and intervertebral-disc v1 newly clip. Right direction, not right yet, and a framing rule has to be proved on the corpus. So I reverted it: sha256(viz3d.js) on the device is a8d39821304aea5393728a5192f48f8900081714d03eefcef554311fb513fc59, byte-for-byte the builder's file. Full per-view before/after for 11 scenes: _review-2026-09-10-r3/review-framing-measurements.json.

3 · THE CLAMP. The floor at controls.minDistance is not the clamp the note asked for and cannot be: it is a distance from the SUBJECT'S CENTRE, so it cannot stop the camera being inside a structure, only inside a small one. On intervertebral-disc views 2 and 3 the camera sits exactly at the floor (1.200), i.e. distanceForBox asked to go closer still. The builder's objection to a ratio-to-whole-scene clamp is also right (cardiac-looping's whole-scene box is two side-by-side hearts). Proposed instead: no tuned constant, bound the fit by the view's own named set — see finding 2.

4 · COVERAGE. The item claims to repair 71 shipped mesh scenes and was measured on 2 scenes of 142. I measured 10 more; 3 of them carry finding 1. tools/measure-view-framing.mjs needs an --all mode and a pass/fail threshold (proposed: clippedAtRest false on every view, and no view at 100.0% of frame height) so this is one command rather than a judgement about which scenes to sample.

5 · tools/test-view-framing-player.mjs IS NOT A GATE. No assertions; exits 0 whatever it finds. Run as committed, today, three times in a row, it prints showAll {dist: 2.089, pulledBack: false} — where BUILD-LOG says it proved 'Show all pulls back out (-> 7.24)'. Diagnosed, and it is NOT the product: with a single waitForTimeout(1200) and no intervening page.evaluate, requestAnimationFrame is throttled in headless and the ease never advances. Sampling the camera every 150ms shows the pull-back completing inside 300ms and landing at 6.774; a 3000ms wait lands at 6.798. Fix the harness, not viz3d.js: settle by polling, then assert, then exit non-zero. Until then the proof section of this item cannot be re-checked by running anything.

6 · TWO TOOL DEFECTS, found by using them. (a) measure-view-framing.mjs writes its harness page to a fixed path models-out/_framing/_player.html, so two runs at once overwrite each other's MEDBANK_CONFIG, every mesh fetch fails CORS from the other run's port, and the scene reports 0 views and ~400 console errors. It produced two false findings before I re-ran serially. Give the page a per-scene name. Under CPU contention the same tool also returns lit:0 for views that are fine — a blank reading is only real if it survives a serial re-run. (b) extent()'s clip detector ignores meshes below 0.5 opacity, so on a view where everything ends up ghosted it returns null and clippedAtRest reads false — blind on 3 of intervertebral-disc's 7 views. When the framebuffer read and the geometric read disagree, believe the pixels.

7 · NOT A DEFECT IN THIS ITEM, DO NOT LET IT BLOCK: the item's central claim holds and it is a large win. carpal-tunnel v3 1.7% -> 24.8% of the canvas lit, kidney v1 2.8% -> 15.8%, intervertebral-disc v1 1.05% -> 9.84%, vertebral-column v6 blank -> 41.5%. Mechanical review all green: node --check, lint-viz3d (every name resolves), validate-scenes 142/142, test-fit-idempotent 8/8, test-view-framing 197 checks 0 fail, console clean on every serial run. Round 2 is about finding 1, not about redoing the work.

CORRECTED THIS RUN. tools/decimate-meshes.mjs bbox gate could not fire: it compared bbox(res.verts,null) to bbox(verts,null), and simplify() keeps live-but-unreferenced vertices that writeBinarySTL can never emit, so the two boxes were equal by construction. items.why: Procedural models are in their own units; BodyParts3D meshes are anatomical millimetres. A scene mixing both providers renders one of them as a speck. NOT urgent — every scene queued here is wholly procedural, including the four cerebellum/brainstem ones, which carry zero mesh refs. It becomes blocking the first time a scene wants procedural detail INSIDE a scanned mesh — a circle of Willis inside a brain. Fix by declaring a model's real-world extent in its module (say, the mm the model's unit box spans) and scaling in the adapter, so scenes and scene authors never see units at all.

items.why: MEASURED IN THE LIVE APP 2026-09-10 while verifying the colour fix on a real 20-part scene. BONE_CEILING (0.78) is applied in the bodyparts3d LOAD path, but applyStyles() later does m.material.color.copy(srgbColor(s.color, ...)) on every structure, which OVERWRITES the clamped colour with the raw authored one. Proof: l2 is authored #f0dfa8, whose brightest channel is 0.94 and should clamp to 0.78 — it renders as exactly #f0dfa8. So the ceiling has never reached a student's screen.
items.note: PRE-EXISTING, NOT A REGRESSION — the same overwrite happened before the colour-space fix, so this is not something the fix introduced and it does NOT block deploying. Deliberately not changed before a deploy: fixing it would darken every bone in all 71 ready scenes, and that is a change to verify on its own, not to smuggle in alongside another one. Decide first whether the ceiling is still wanted at all: it was introduced to stop near-white bone clipping under the lights, and correct colour handling already makes bone darker than it was, so the problem it guarded against may simply be gone.
